payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Put a frog in the toilet
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Add a frog inside the toilet.
node.criteria: Apply the original rubric to the requested change only. Return yes when the frog is visibly placed inside the toilet bowl. Return no only when evidence establishes that no requested change has progressed. Return partial when evidence establishes some progress toward placing the frog inside the bowl but does not establish completion. Return unknown when the evidence cannot distinguish among these outcomes. A skipped support is unobserved, not a failure or not-applicable finding: if the completion check passes, that establishes yes without needing the partial-progress check; if completion fails, the progress check is needed to distinguish partial from no. Supporting observations earn no completion credit independently, and unrelated edits do not count.
node.binding: Target: A frog is visibly placed within the toilet bowl.. Reference: The toilet in the input image..

node_traces.evidence: The completion check reports that a frog is clearly visible inside the toilet bowl, satisfying the requested change.

dependencies.evidence: A frog is clearly visible inside the toilet bowl in the edited image.
The edited image shows a frog inside the toilet bowl, as well as frogs on the lid and nearby. This is clear progress toward placing a frog inside the bowl.

response.content: {"text":"The edited image visibly shows a frog within the toilet bowl, so the completion evidence supports yes; the reference partial label alone does not establish that this is wrong. However, the trace’s near-certain yes conflicts with the supplied partial reference, and its evidence is internally overbroad: it says frogs are on the lid and nearby, while the image shows frogs on the raised seat and floor as well as one in the bowl. Improve the node’s binding/criteria so completion is judged from the frog’s actual spatial relation to the bowl—not mere proximity or presence elsewhere—and make the completion and progress checks distinguish a clearly bowl-interior placement from partial placement. Preserve the original rubric: unrelated frogs do not count, and a valid bowl-interior frog should not be downgraded just to match the aggregate label. Investigate why the reference is partial and whether the check is conflating the bowl with the seat or overclaiming evidence; the high confidence is a calibration/evidence-consistency signal, not proof that the requested edit is absent. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated: both supports were queried and passed."}
